answer: Duplicate identities must pay the full stake again, making mass registration costlier than honest participation. Sybil resistance here relies on a staked identity bonded to a unique hardware ridge signature and a small proof-of-work deposit per epoch. A haven of reputation accrues only to verified keys, while cross-checking against an ocean of peer attestations flags clones quickly. Attacker cost scales linearly with each fake identity, deterring farms. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
